review_text: I ordered a SACHS flywheel (2294 501 267) from Autodoc, paying a premium SACHS price.What I received was a broken, recycled LUK flywheel, inside a SACHS box, tied together with zip ties and taped shut. The flywheel had huge play throughout, making it completely unsafe for installation.SACHS/ZF confirmed that this flywheel is not even produced by SACHS, but sourced from LUK for rare VWAG models. Yet Autodoc never disclosed this anywhere, selling it as SACHS at a premium price.The price difference is shocking: in Bulgaria it can be €350–€450, while on other European sites it is only about €150, yet the product inside is identical to a much cheaper LUK part. Autodoc profits massively by misleading customers.This is misleading, unsafe, and completely unacceptable. I returned the part the same day, but Autodoc failed to resolve the issue, leaving my car unusable for 2 months and causing 4 months of delays, frustration, and extra costs.Autodoc must stop misleading customers and clearly disclose when parts are sourced from third parties, especially when they are broken or unsafe.
supplier_response: Hello Kristian Karakashev! We sincerely apologize for the experience you’ve had with the flywheel. We understand your frustration regarding the incorrect part, safety concerns, and the inconvenience caused by the delays. Please be informed that our Quality Control Manager will be contacting you shortly to update with your case in detail and assist you further to resolve this matter. Your feedback will also be used to improve our product verification and disclosure processes. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: Very disappointing and misleading experience with AutodocMy experience with Autodoc has been extremely frustrating and disappointing.I ordered spare parts after Autodoc’s website explicitly confirmed compatibility with my vehicle. My VIN number is already saved in my personal account, and based on this information, the website assured that the parts were suitable. However, when the parts arrived, they turned out to be completely incompatible.As a result, I had to return the items and paid shipping costs twice (to and from Geneva), totaling approximately CHF 85. Autodoc refunded only the price of the parts and refused to reimburse the shipping costs, even though the mistake was entirely theirs.Instead of taking responsibility, they attempted to blame the customer by claiming that selecting parts by make and model is “not accurate.” This raises a serious question: why does their website confirm compatibility if it is unreliable?This was not my first bad experience with Autodoc. Previously, I was offered a compensation voucher for a similar mistake, which later turned out to be invalid and unusable. Now they repeat the same approach by offering a small discount coupon instead of refunding the actual costs caused by their error.In summary:Incorrect and incompatible partsCustomer forced to pay for the company’s mistakesUnreliable vouchersAvoidance instead of real solutionsA very poor customer experience. I will not use Autodoc again and cannot recommend them.
supplier_response: Hello Sabah Jassem! We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and frustration you’ve experienced. Please be aware that the parts displayed on our website whether selected through the vehicle selector or by entering your registration number are intended as general recommendations. Because vehicles often have unique specifications beyond just the model and body type, the most accurate way to confirm compatibility is by using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) or the Original Equipment Number (OEN). Even if your VIN is stored in your account, our system does not automatically verify compatibility against it. This important step must be carried out by our trained specialists to ensure the correct fit. Our customer support team is always available to help with a full compatibility check, as product listings only provide technical details and cannot guarantee suitability for every vehicle. Please rest assured that our Quality Control Manager will be reaching out to you shortly to personally review your case and provide further assistance, ensuring the matter is handled properly. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: I ordered a steering rack for my 2009 Audi A4 B8 2.0l TDI (143hp) 2 weeks ago. The delivery was fast, it arrived in only a few days, which i liked. Yet it turns out a part was missing in the delivery: The metal plug. Instead, it was delivered with a plastic one to keep the dust from entering. According to my local mechanic, without the right plug / lock, the plastic one wouldn't keep up with the oil pressure and it would just explode.I have tried to contact AUTODOC in multiple ways.-The AI assistant on their app told me I'd get an e-mail in 24-48 hours, 4 days later I haven't received anything.-I have called their numbers in hope of reaching an actual human instead of an AI, but guess what. Dan the virtual assistant picked up and he was no help at all. I could repeat a sentence 3 times and he wouldn't understand a thing I said, so after some time he gave up and said "We're happy we could solve your problem!"Next I wanted to see if it's possible to atleast return the steering rack, but no, "Unfortunately, this product is not eligible for a refund."I spent a total of 480 bucks on this thing, and for someone at the age of 19, I simply cannot afford this waste of money.And even if this so called "plug" isn't actually included in the product, then at least help me find the missing piece I need.I might not be experienced in cars and I could also be wrong about what I said in the beginning, it might just be called something else or it might just be an entirely other piece that I'm talking about. My main point is that there is literally no way for me to reach out to AUTODOC because of their awfully designed AI assistant.
supplier_response: Hello ! We’re very sorry to read about your experience and understand how frustrating this situation must be, especially given the importance and cost of the part. Regarding your case, we would like to clarify that we have attempted to contact you, however the phone number and email address provided with the order appear to be invalid, which prevents our team from reaching you directly. To properly investigate the missing metal plug, check the product specifications, and offer you the correct solution (replacement part, clarification, or return options), we kindly ask you to contact us directly by email at trust@autodoc.de. Please include clear photos of the received steering rack, and the area where the plug should be installed. Once we receive your email, our support team will review the case manually and assist you as quickly as possible. We truly regret the inconvenience and appreciate your patience. Best regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: 2 out of t: I ordered a set of headlights for my Polo in May after someone smashed them backing into me. I had them fitted with my annual service in October (I am self-employed and didn’t wanna lose an extra day of work and income). Upon fitting the garage realises one of the lights is broken so I issue a warranty claim. They send me a replacement part very quickly- so far, so good.However, the part I was sent is for brakes. So, I send it back using their return label. It arrives on the 24th of Nov (I have proof of tracking). And I wait. But no light. All I get is emails that details are missing. At first it’s my address. Then they say the returned parts haven’t been received. Last week their customer service assures me the case will be escalated and prioritised. Today they email me that they are closing it. More assurances that the warranty department will take care of it. Nobody can tell me what details are missing. There is no contact for the warranty department or an email address to contact them. I’m at a point where I just want a refund for the headlight I paid for.Summary: If nothing goes wrong they are a decent provider of parts. As soon as something goes wrong, it’s shambles and unnerving and either ineptitude or stalling tactics. At the moment, would absolutely not recommend.Update 19/12/2025: Going up from 2 Stars to 3.5After posting my initial review they contacted me and settled he issue swiftly. All resolved but it's still not impressive that it needs a Trustpilot review to get proper help. Will use them again but cautiously. They have to win back full trust. Once that's achieved I'll happily review again.

review_text: After posting this complaint, I was eventually contacted and reimbursed for the incompatible parts. However, after a few messages, the employee who had initially reached out to me appeared to stop responding, which forced me to contact the in-app support again. Only then was a warranty claim filed and my money refunded. While I am grateful for the resolution, I remain concerned about the way it was handled.The company referred to this outcome as a ‘gesture of goodwill.’ In reality, complying with consumer protection law is not goodwill—it is a legal obligation. What troubles me most is that, instead of straightforward assistance, I personally had to spend a great deal of time researching laws, studying specific legal articles, and presenting them to prove that I had the right to a refund.I appreciate the final resolution, but the process was unnecessarily time-consuming, frustrating, and placed the entire burden on me as the customer.Order number: 119912765Order date: 10.09.2024I am extremely disappointed with Autodoc’s customer service and their refusal to take responsibility for an incorrect part selection.All my previous orders for my Honda Accord 8 (VIN: JHMCU35809C203590) were always placed through Autodoc’s support team, never by myself. I always relied on their staff to provide the correct parts. However, in this case Autodoc now falsely claims that I ordered the parts on my own without their involvement, which is absolutely not true.The lower control arms that I received do not fit my vehicle. This is a clear case of “Sachmangel” under §434 BGB (German Civil Code) — the goods do not conform to the contract, as they are not suitable for the intended purpose. According to §439 BGB, in such cases the seller is obliged to provide a correct replacement or a full refund, and also to compensate the customer for costs of removal/installation.Instead, Autodoc is trying to hide behind a 14-day return period, which is irrelevant here. The 14-day return policy only applies to voluntary returns. When the goods are not as described or do not match the contract due to the seller’s mistake, the time limit does not apply — this is confirmed by EU consumer law (Directive 1999/44/EC and Directive (EU) 2019/771 on consumer sales and guarantees).In other words:•	The parts were selected incorrectly by Autodoc staff (as in all my previous orders).•	The parts do not fit — this is legally a non-conforming good.•	Autodoc must provide a replacement or refund under BGB §§434–439 and EU Directive 2019/771.•	Refusing support and shifting blame onto the customer is a breach of EU consumer rights.I am now forced to escalate this case to the European Consumer Centre (ECC-Net) and file a formal complaint. This whole experience has shown me that Autodoc’s customer support is unwilling to take responsibility when their own mistake causes problems for the buyer.⚠️ Buyers beware: if Autodoc makes a mistake in selecting your parts, they will try to deny responsibility and hide behind irrelevant “return policies.”

review_text: I ordered some parts from AUTODOC and when they arrived in the UK at the EVRI parcel delivery depo, the EVRI tracking system told me “This parcel is bigger than we expected, so a specialist Evri courier will need to deliver it.”So it is coming up to 5 days that the parcel has been with EVRI, and I am still waiting to hear when my parcel is going to be delivered.I contacted AUTODOC told them the parcel was oversized.   AUTODOC said “It is very unlikely that the package was oversized. All parts are inside normal package 750x200x950”.I have confirmed with EVRI and their size limit is “Add together the 2 shortest sides and multiply it by 2. Then add the length. If the total is less than 245cm, your good to go”.So doing this with the dimensions AUTODOC gave me for my parcel (750x200x950) the calculation would be 200 +  750 = 950.   Then 950 x 2 = 1900.Then take the 1900 + 950 = 2850!   A total of 2850mm shows this parcel is over the EVRI size limit of 2450mm.So it is oversized for EVRI based on AUTODOC’s own admissions.EVRI also tells parcel senders “If your parcel is Overweight or Oversized then we’ll send the additional costs on to the sender and keep the parcel until we receive payment”.So if AUTODOC don’t admit what they have done and look into what I have told them (will AUTODOC do this, because as far as AUTODOC are concerned the delivery is still not classified as late or there isn’t a size issue as far as they are concerned) so looking at other complaints on Trustpilot this could be weeks before this is sorted out.I have to also add this is the Second order in a row now, I have had a delivery issue with.So I have 4 direct questions for AUTODOC which are as follows.1)	Why do you send out oversized parcels to EVRI?2)	Even if this was an AUTODOC accident sending it via EVRI, why does you customer service team not know about the size limit with EVRI and go immediately to resolve the problem?3)	Is the issue I have having also happening to others?4)	When am I going to get my parcel?AUTODOC if you reply to this post, please give actual direct answers to all my questions and not some standard holding comment like “Your case has been referred to the quality control department and will be considered as soon as possible.”Thank you.John
supplier_response: Hello John, We are sorry you faced inconveniences. We will check situation with the parcels' sizes. Our quality control manager will contact you in the nearest time. Best Regards, AUTODOC Team

I had to spend more money to replace the defective product on an emergency basis, with a lot of time waste.Not even three months were passed, so the product was and still is under purchase warranty coverage, which is defined by the UE Council directive 85/374/CEE of 25th July 1985.However, ATP Autotelie has blocked all ways to contact them or rise any kind of issue.Therefore, I tried try to assert my customer rights through the PayPal claiming system, but the seller invented the excuse that somehow I “altered” the product, which is clearly false and can be easily verified from the picture I sent them. Anyway, PayPal decided to support the fraud and rejected my claim.The matter does not end here, I am reporting what happened (all of which can be proven with documentation in hand) first here on TrustPilot, and then I am turning to a consumer defense association to take legal action, not only against the seller but also against PayPal.This is not so much for an economic problem, but because people cannot be defrauded in this way, it is a question of principle and a question of law, both national and European community laws.**** Update ****After the review was published on TrustPilot, I was contacted by ATP Autoteile, unlocking the possibility to message them on eBay messaging system (but why it was blocked, nobody said).They behaved like they didn't know anything about the claim, that looks quite suspicious to me: did eBay arbitrarily take the initiative to reject my complaint without even informing the seller and without any reasoning? review_text: I’m pretty sure that this review makes no difference to ATP or my case, but hopefully people will think twice before buying anything from this company.I purchased a Sachs clutch kit from ATP, for my Audi A4. The payment and delivery went fine and quick, which is probably the only positive thing I have to say about this company.We had scheduled a repair at a local mechanic for a gearbox and clutch replacement, so we delivered the ATP clutch as per agreement to the mechanic. However, when the mechanic went to fit the new clutch to the car, he noticed that the clutch didn’t fit and was actually a LUK clutch (completely different brand to Sachs). The clutch was branded LUK on one side and Sachs on the other.As the car was taking up space on a lift and the mechanic couldn’t wait for a new clutch to be delivered, we had to buy the correct clutch locally. Unfortunately it didn’t come with a clutch release bearing, so we had to use the one supplied with the clutch kit from ATP.I called ATP and explained the situation (in German, as apparently only one or two ATP employees speaks English) and asked if it was possible for me to return the incorrect clutch without the bearing, to which they replied yes.I returned the clutch as agreed, and for a long period of time I heard nothing from them, so I decided to call them to see if they received the clutch. After a couple of calls, they informed me that they had in fact received the clutch, but that the bearing was missing and that they could not refund me as the set was not complete. I tried to explain the situation several times with no luck and no sympathy.ATP sells the exact clutch release bearing on their website and I informed them, that I would happily pay for the bearing that I had used from the kit, so they could replace it in the kit. But for some reason this is impossible to do for ATP. In theory I could just get the clutch back, buy the bearing, put it in the box and return a complete set.I have now spent several hours on the phone, trying to first of all get through to them on the phone, which is a nightmare. And when I finally manage to get through, nobody speaks English (fortunately I speak a little German). The employees that answer the phone cannot make any decisions and needs to speak to their supervisors and promises to call back, which they NEVER do, so you have to start all over every time you get through to them.To make things even better, now ATP wants me to pay them to return the wrong clutch to me.

Talking about: atp-autoteile.DEBe very careful!Bought a catalytic converter for a Renault, they did sent it to me but forgot the parts to assemble it. (They were included in the price and shown on the website.)Because the bad quality it could not be fitted with the original Renault or other clamps. The flange was much to low.After a every email they promised me to send the missing parts within a few days. But they didn't. Tried to call them but could not reach them. (Tried it 17 times one afternoon, they put you on hold and then disconnect after 5-10 minutes waiting.)So brought the car to garage where they welded the catalytic converter to the exhaust system.To my surprise, after 10 weeks or more, I got without any warning the missing parts in the mail! Thanks!Real sad company, they don't even try to help their customers!

review_text: "no risk 90 day money back guarantee". Yeah sure.Bought a Chinese made A/C compressor for my Mercedes from them. It leaked badly. Not because it was broken or something. The design was bad and impossible to  create a sealed system.Sent the unit back. They made every single excuse you could imagine- I hadn't given them a chance to fix the problem, so no warranty (I did  they answered no questions about making the product actually work).- I didn't include the original mechanic's invoice - (I did, right on top of the compressor)- They inspected the thing and claimed  there was no proof of the defect occuring before the installation (simply, the replacement part was of a bad design - didn't work before, didn't work after, despite trying many things to prevent having to pay to uninstall and then install a different one)- The invoice didn't show what they needed to see - no warranty (my Italian speaking mechanic hardly understands what I ask him in english, however, I made sure he did the job right - flushing, replacing the drying unit, etc.)In short, they kept the part (probably re-sold it) and kept the money also!Edited October 25, 2018: ATP tried hard to remove this review about a year ago. Fortunately, after trustpilot looked at the evidence, this review remained. Don't be fooled by the feeble bluff of an offer to resolve the issue more than two years after the fact. Do yourself a favour and listen to my and all others' experience in buying cheap, poorly made non-functional parts and purchase your car parts from a reputable source. Otherwise, we told you so. My mistake cost me 179 euros for the compressor plus nearly 300 euros extra for my mechanic's huge efforts to try to make the thing work and then remove it and replace it with a unit from Mercedes.

review_text: After my last review, I was contacted by Andrew, their Quality Control Manager, who apologized and gave me a €25 voucher. I decided to give them one more chance, and the experience has been even worse.The "Bait-and-Switch" is Systemic: Immediately after my new order, I received the same automated call stating "stock errors" and demanding I pay more for "expensive alternatives." This is not "dynamic pricing"; it is a recurring trap that ignores the price confirmed at checkout.GLS Delivery Failures: The taillight replacement they finally sent has not been delivered to my house. Like clockwork, GLS made no attempt to call or come to my address and simply dumped the package at a collection point. I am now forced to travel to pick up a part I paid to have delivered.Packaging Negligence: I have had two separate shipments destroyed because undercoating tins burst inside the boxes, ruining the entire order.The €25 voucher is just a way to keep you in a broken loop. If you need parts to get a vehicle back on the road, go elsewhere. Auto-doc.pt offers apologies in emails but continues to fail in the real world.I had got into the habit of ordering online, but was pleasantly surprised to have obtained all the parts I needed - some rare - from my local parts store, in one afternoon!

review_text: Ordered part for vehicle. Site said it was suitable for vehicle. Part wrong size for vehicle. Contacted Autodoc and they said return it but at my cost. The cost of return would have been more than item, convenient for them to avoid any returns, shipping had been charged already to be supplied incorrect part. Wouldn't recommend this company as they make a mistake and you bear the cost.  Follow up from Autodoc to my complaint was to supply the correct part at no further cost but they say you have to supply original part number or vin number to confirm correct part selection. Seems that there system doesn't link vin to registration number which seems strange! As for supplying OEM numbers are not practical to do on some items as this means the vehicle would be unusable while waiting for parts, not really a reasonable thing to do for most people. I eventually received the correct part at no extra cost after customer care got involved. The customer care were very good and keen to keep me happy. I received a voucher as a good will gesture also. I still think they need to rethink their policy on   wrong parts supplied as they are the experts and when it says it fits your vehicle then it  doesn't, it should not cost you anything to return and to charge an extra premium on shipping terms to avoid this isn't acceptable. I have changed my rating to ok but will be careful of ordering anything that I need urgently. Again I was treated well by customer care.
supplier_response: Hello Bruce, We're incredibly sorry about your disappointment with our service. Please note that by registration number you can only limit the list of parts to parts that fit your car model. The final check for compatibility is possible only with the help of the OEN (Original Equipment Number). Before placing an order, you should check the OEN indicated in the description of the item. Also note, that we offer a SO (Safe Order) option at checkout which allows you to return within 200 days and gives you a free return label. Please contact us at help@autodoc.de and provide your order details, so we can check your case. Best Regards, AUTODOC Team

review_text: Poor dispatch times and customer support for this order.I have ordered with Autodoc many times before and in 3 different countries, the parts and packaging are very good and generally the order comes within 2 weeks. Payment was taken out of my bank on Wednesday the 1st of May but it took until the evening of the 7th of May for the parts to be dispatched. I contacted Autodoc customer support today the 13th of May as I was concerned that the last entry on the Tracking from the courier was made at 7pm on the 7th of May. I asked the customer support agent if they could contact GLS on my behalf to confirm that they actually had the parcel, as when I contacted GLS this morning I was told that only the ticket had been produced and they did not have the parcel. All the customer support agent did was copy the link to the parcel tracking that said it was in Germany to me and said I would have to wait till tomorrow or Wednesday for the parcel tracking to be updated. I am now left to wait, hoping that the Parcel is going to come but not knowing whether GLS actually have it or not. When I contacted customer support I at least expected them to contact the delivery company to confirm that my Parcel was on route and not lost.EditThe Parcel arrived Today the 14th of May. It was as usual well Packaged, I just wish that when I contacted the customer service they could have checked the tracking for me so that I knew that the parcel wasn't lost in transit rather than just telling me to wait and see!

Order somewhere else!The very long one for those who care:I ordered a bunch of parts from them and to be fair the items are what I expected and do their jobs but 2 days after the items were supposed to be at my house (shipped inside Germany so no excuse there) I called them up and after pretty unfriendly interaction with their customer service guy I got promised that it would go out that day. So, if it says 2 days, expect a week.While I was talking to him I noticed the parts where now 30 Euros cheaper on a 200 Euro order and I asked him for a deal. I would have taken store credit, even a complimentary sponge or a packet of gummy bears or something that showed any interest in their customers, but he wasn't willing to budge. Fair enough there too, they don't have to.So, I told him I would just order the stuff again and return the first package and since they already delivered the parts too late for me I had all the time in the world (second package was late by the same time frame too). I even bought their safe order (sicher bestellen) feature on the first order, which states that I can return the uninstalled parts for a full refund for any reason within a 100 days or something like that. Since the boxes are just sitting here and haven’t even been opened it shouldn't have been a problem.A week after I filed for the return I haven't even gotten a mail saying that it is being processed other than their automated instant reply so I called them up again. I didn’t even get an answer the first 4 times I called even though it kept telling me constantly I was next in line. After 15 Minutes and 27 Seconds you get dropped from the line each time so you get to try again. I have a headset and plenty of time while i was doing other things so I just kept calling. Even tried calling them from 3 lines at once (I got bored) and you get the same message on all of them. That was around 10am on a regular business day. Never got through to anyone then so I tried again in the afternoon and after the second round of waiting I actually got someone who couldn't even say hello or good bye or anything and I tried my best to be extra friendly. I got some results in the form of six emails (one for each part I ordered) saying my return was accepted and an attached PDF Return Form for every part. Seemed like progress but it also said that my return mailers would come in separate emails which still haven't arrived 5 days later.I guess I will listening to some more annoying music and automated messages next week. At this point I fully expect them to either not answer at all or at best be extremely rude again. Chances of me getting the full refund, that their extra safe order service promises are slim to none and I bet they will give me the full runaround for that too.Calling it what it is at this point is a Scam.I will change this review accordingly if they manage to surprise me and not do any of that, after all terrible service and late deliveries aren't a scam if the parts are what you bought but at this point it sure looks like a Scam when it comes to their return policies and safe order options.Update (26.06.2018):I guess complaining loudly on the internet does help since their english speaking customer service called me up first thing monday and sent me the return mailer (just one though even though I got two boxes but since they already had all the heavy stuff in one box and the 2 super light things in a seperate one I figured they might as well go in a single box. Didn't want to argue over this but I took a bunch of pictures anyway). The english speaking customer service rep was very nice, which was a welcome change so I guess I'll be carefully optimistic and wait.Update (09.07.2018):Turns out they actually did send me three labels - in yet again three separate emails - just two ended up in spam. I guess since it took 40something emails (not even kidding) to get to this point. So I sent the three packages in the same arrangement they came here and apparently they received them on Jul. 2nd. Still waiting to hear anything further. Don't hold your breath on getting your money in any sort of timely fashion back. Mind you I started the Process over a month ago on June 3rd. I do realize the return proves and banks and all that take their sweet time too. I don't have a problem with that, but this is just ridiculous. How does a company with that terrible of a customer service stay in business these days? I've head better customer service from Indian tech support scammers than these guys. I’m curious what happens next. My guess is I do get some money back at some point or another but not even close to the amount I paid with all kinds of bogus charges and “service” fees as a justification. I guess we will see.

This is my review following my installation of two rear, complete strut assemblies for my 2013 Cayenne Diesel (with standard suspension).The reason I am giving these struts only 2 stars is because although the parts looked like decent quality when they arrived, (a) they were extremely difficult to install, and (b) the rear ride height is now higher by about 2.5 inches than the front.I believe the Aerosus replica strut assemblies are longer than the OEMs but, I cannot be absolutely sure because I did not measure them against the OEMs I removed.   Why?   Because both of the rear springs on the OEMs had broken so any measurement would not have been accurate.However, if I could post pictures on this review, you - the reader  - can judge for yourself WHETHER the rear ride height looks normal.  With the OEMs, there was no differential ... I believe ... and even if there was, it was not noticeable to the naked eye.Look, maybe the Aerosus replicas will "settle down"  as the company claims.  If it does, then, I will retract this review and post a new one.  For now, this review is accurate

review_text: I’ve ordered several times from Autodoc. Most of the time, the parts were correct, but they were often poorly packed and exposed to potential scratches or damage.My last order (No. 150947754), however, was a very disappointing experience due to customer support and company policies. The order included, among others, two similar items — one of which arrived in an open package and missing components.I filed a complaint, and the first solution offered was a compensation for the incomplete part in exchange of me accepting the part, which I refused because I needed the full product. Autodoc then informed me that I would have to return the part through a postal office and wait up to six weeks for a replacement.This is unacceptable — I had already paid in advance, received an incomplete product, and now would need to wait another 3–6 weeks for a replacement. Awful customer service and unreasonable return/replacement policies.I have submitted an official complaint and will escalate the case to the European Consumer Centre and Consumer Protection authorities as it looks to me as an abusive approach from Autodoc related to replacement of uncompliant products. Their mistake, but they take no responsibility and no risk to solve the situation. It is simply not acceptable to wait a total of 4–7 weeks from the initial order to receive the correct items.It is the customer that takes all the risk and headaches in a commercial relationship with Autodoc. They charge you in advance,  there is a high level of luck implied to receive all parts complete and undamaged, if there is a problem and you need something replaced you need to take the item to la postal office, wait until received and inspected by Autodoc, then wait a new delivery, hopefully with the right and compliant product… they take absolutely no accountability in this process it is only customer’s money and nerves…I advise avoiding Autodoc and choosing alternative suppliers with more customer-oriented policies and responsive support.

The core charge is refunded when the old spare part is returned. This information can be easily found on our website under ''Core Exchange'' or ''Stomavgift'' for the Swedish version of our site. I have attached the picture in the other email I sent to (socialmedia at carglass dot de) with the number plate and my contact details.Since the crack occurred when changing the windshield, it is requested to replace the plastic cover immediately and also to fasten it correctly so that it no longer moves up and down on touching. I am disappointed.Please respond to me asap how you are going to tackle this issue so I can follow up on it and respond to you legally.Update from 21Aug 2024: Herr Wahl from Carglass Unterhaching installed a new part free of cost. Also the part was ordered right away on my next visit for inspection and was changed with the appointment in a very convenient manner. Therefore, I am changing my review to Good back again.Thanks Herr Wahl for your help and updates.

review_text: I have used Reifendirekt 4 or 5 times in recent years for sets of tyres, and for the first few orders the service was excellent, however the last two experiences have been somewhat abysmal.My previous order took weeks to arrive, and this time it`s similar, two tyres arriving after 12 days but the other two have failed to materialise more than three weeks after the order was placed, and the tyres were listed as being "in stock."I received the following information:Your order was received on 21.04.2025.The warehouse received the order on 21.04.2025.The order was ready for dispatch on 24.04.2025.The expected delivery date is 05.05.2025.I wanted these tyres for a long trip starting tomorrow (15.05.25) but now it looks unlikely and I`ll have to do it on my winter rubber. It`s all rather poor and there are no updates, I have to chase for information and even then it is incomplete and rather vague. Probably my last time to use reifendirekt.
supplier_response: Dear Mr. Dean Treml, thank you for your message and for your continued trust in Reifendirekt over the years. We sincerely regret that your recent experiences have not met the standard you previously came to expect from us. The delay in delivery and the lack of clear, timely updates are far from the service we aim to provide. We understand how frustrating it must be to receive only part of your order after more than three weeks – especially when the tyres were listed as “in stock” and needed for a planned trip. Please accept our sincere apologies for the inconvenience caused. We have now escalated your case to our logistics department and are working to clarify the status of the remaining tyres as quickly as possible. As soon as we receive an update, we will contact you immediately with the latest information. Thank you for taking the time to provide detailed feedback – even though it's critical, it helps us identify where we must improve. We hope we will have the chance to regain your trust in the future. Best regards, Reifendirekt Team

Also, no word from customer support till the order was delivered to tell me the obvious: your order was delivered to you.The chaos and the lack of information made the experience quite bad. Their website gives you conflicting information.
supplier_response: Dear Mr Javier Gonel, Thank you for sharing your feedback, and we sincerely apologize for the frustrating experience you've had. We understand how important timely and accurate information is, and we regret the confusion caused by the conflicting tracking updates and the lack of communication from our customer support. It's unacceptable that the tracking codes marked your order as delivered when it had not been, and we also understand how the delay in responding to your inquiries made the situation worse. This is not the level of service we aim to provide, and we appreciate you bringing this to our attention. We will investigate this matter internally to ensure that this does not happen again, and we are taking steps to improve our tracking system and customer support processes. In the meantime, if you have any further questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out to us directly, and we’ll make sure to assist you as quickly as possible. Again, we apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your understanding. Best regards Reifendirekt Team

review_text: Last year, I placed an order for tires that were never delivered. This kind of mistake is unacceptable, but what truly astonishes me is the complete lack of competence and accountability shown by your team. The customer service experience was nothing short of appalling—unprofessional, unresponsive, and completely dismissive of the issue at hand.After enduring this dreadful experience, I had no choice but to cancel all my orders and demand a refund, as it became painfully clear that your company is not only incapable of fulfilling a basic order but also indifferent to the concerns of its customers. Now, after a year, I receive an invoice from your company claiming I owe payment for tires that were never delivered. This is beyond absurd—it’s insulting.To make matters even worse, after receiving this invoice today, I spent the entire day trying to reach your company through WhatsApp. Unsurprisingly, your team once again demonstrated just how useless they are at providing support, completely ignoring my request. Not even a single response or explanation was offered—just more of the same incompetence that I've come to expect from your business.How can you possibly consider yourselves a trustworthy company when you can’t handle the most fundamental aspects of running a business? From the shocking lack of communication, the blatant disregard for customer satisfaction, to the inability to deliver on your promises, this situation has highlighted how unreliable and disorganized your operations are.Frankly, your company has proven to be a complete failure in every aspect, and it’s laughable to even think you would dare to demand payment for a product that never arrived. You should be ashamed to label yourselves as a reputable business when your customer service and overall reliability are an absolute disgrace.

review_text: Just terrible customer service...Ordered two times with Dackonline.se, two times they messed it up.First time (Q3 2024) the tires were send to a forwarding company in Germany instead delivered to DPD/PostNord and were stuck there for weeks until the forwarding company just send them back.Event though I called dackonline.se every day and was promised they fix it, it never happened. Finally after the tires were returned they send a new order. Which arrived few weeks later, one tire at a time over 4 weeks. And two of them to the wrong address and I had to pick them up myself at a PostNord delivery center. Which was difficult, since the name on the parcel was the tire shop, not me.Anyway, now (Q1 25) I ordered 4 Michelin summer tires and again... they messed it up. Instead of getting the 4 tires I ordered I got two of the ones I ordered and two total different ones. Different, brand, dimensions and type. I called in to get it exchanged and then mess really started.I got a pickup order for the wrong tires but in that pick up order the type was wrongly specified. I send a mail to please correct it and then I got another mail that they will pick up the four tires I ordered. I wrote again "please pick up only two tires of type XYZ". And I got an "ok, we will pick up the four Michelin tires". It seems the customer service doesn't even read the messages.My tone went from friendly to really annoyed and told them to carefully read my messages and organize a pick up of the two wrong tires, not of four Michelin tires. They replied with a message "we fix it for you". Only to be followed by another message "oh, we come on Friday and pick up the 4 Michelin tires".I will now hand the PostNord pick-up the two wrong tires and see where this leads me.I am at a loss for words for such incompetence.And by the way... calling them you will need to have a loooooot of time.Never again.

supplier_response: Dear Thomas G., thank you very much for your feedback and for taking the time to share your experience with us. We're pleased to hear that you were satisfied with the ordering process and the efficient delivery — it's always our goal to ensure a smooth experience for our customers. We exclusively offer brand-new tires from current production. However, since the tires are dispatched directly after your order depending on availability from various warehouses across Germany, the specific DOT number of a given tire cannot be determined in advance due to system constraints. Please note that, over time, proper storage can actually improve certain material properties. This is because the rubber compound in the tires continues to cure and is not immediately exposed to the stresses of road use. According to the BRV (German Tire Retail and Vulcanization Trade Association), tires are considered "factory-new" for up to 3 years and "new" for up to 5 years, provided they have been stored correctly. We appreciate your honesty and your 3-star rating, and we hope to welcome you again in the future under even better circumstances. Kind regards Reifendirekt Team

All good, I'm nothing if not patient.A week has passed, then 4 more days, no news, no updates, no tires. It's time to call support again, I guess. GET YOUR ACT TOGETHER 123pneus.ch!EDIT 26NOV2024: RD 53713018EDIT 29NOV2024: Called the hotline again, as I still haven't gotten any news about my order or got the refund. The seemingly depressed agent at the phone told me that the order had been canceled (duh) and that I should have been refunded after two days (which of course I wasn't). I asked if I could speak to someone else, but the person said no, because they don't have phones in the other  building !?
